messages:
maya: FYI staging p95 jumped ~2.3x after the model-onboard merge (checkpoint v3.1). Noticing lots of KV cache evictions and unusually small batch sizes.
devon: saw that too. Any idea if tokenizer changed padding/encoding?
sasha: ran a quick profile on a few requests. Kernel chooser is routing long-tail minibatches to the fallback kernel instead of the q8f_opt kernel. Sample from perf trace: `kernel_choice=fallback_slow (latency 48ms)` where previous was `q8f_opt (12ms)`.
maya: exact symptoms: early tokens look fine, after 64 tokens we see p99 jump and KV cache miss rate spikes. Could be tokenizer producing different tokenization boundaries, changing avg seq len distribution and invalidating batching heuristics.
ci-bot: BUILD-PERF: staging-checkpoint-onboard #412 failed perf threshold (p95 > 120ms) for job: inference-e2e-staging. Link: https://ci.internal/jobs/412
devon: ran `git bisect` across the onboard merges — pointing at commit abcd1234 (tokenizer: switch to new encoder->utf8-normalization).
sasha: profiling snippets: `alloc profile: kv_cache.evictions: 230/s`, `batching: avg_batch=1.6`, `kernel_selector: score[q8f_opt]=0.32, score[fallback]=0.68`. Also saw `kv_prefetch` disabled for that route.
lin: hmm, tokenizer change could increase number of subtokens per prompt (more tokens for same input) leading to different sequence-length histogram that breaks our batcher thresholds. Did we update `batcher.window_ms` or `batcher.max_seqlen`?
maya: no config change in deploy besides the checkpoint + tokenizer. Batcher config same. I suspect the kernel selector's heuristics expect a median seq len < 128. New tokenizer pushes median to ~180 for some doc types.
ravi: quick mitigation: can we force kernel routing to q8f_opt for this model via routing override? That would avoid fallback but might saturate memory.
sasha: tried manual override on a shadow instance: routes to q8f_opt reduce p95 to ~14ms but memory pressure increased 30% and KV cache warmup took longer. But still better than fallback.
devon: plan: 1) patch batcher to use dynamic windowing based on observed seq_len histogram, 2) tweak kernel_selector to compute expected mem footprint using tokenizer histogram, 3) re-enable kv_prefetch for first N requests to avoid cold-eviction storm.
maya: +1. Also we should block the rollout for dedicated staging until we validate. Marking as rollout blocker.
sasha: created flamegraph and uploaded to /artifacts/flame_1988881234.svg (private). Key stack shows `kernel_choice` time at 65% of extra latency.
ci-bot: NOTE: perf regression triage required for job #412. Assigning to @maya and @sasha.
ravi: I'm opening PRs: 1) batcher: dynamic-window heuristic (WIP) 2) kernel-selector: add tokenizer-histogram input (WIP). Will link PRs here.
devon: did bisect confirm tokenizer encoder change is the root cause or an enabler? Might be the combination: encoder + a recent scheduler tweak.
sasha: bisect pointer shows later scheduler tweak (commit ef12c9) made the batcher stop increasing window when median length > 150, so both are in play.
lin: suggest short-term revert: revert commit ef12c9 from staging so batcher resumes previous behavior while we land more robust heuristics.
maya: agree. Revert staged now? If revert reduces p95 below threshold we can un-block rollout.
ci-bot: DEPLOY: Revert request submitted by maya for ef12c9. Tracking: revert-1988881234.
ravi: PRs posted: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/918 (batcher) and /pulls/919 (kernel-selector). Including tests and perf benchmark.
sasha: test run on shadow with revert + kernel-override shows p95 back to ~13ms and KV evictions down 80%.
maya: OK lets hold rollout until revert is in and we run 24h shadow. Assign owners: revert = maya, longterm fixes = ravi + sasha, monitoring dashboard tweak = lin.
devon: created incident doc: https://wiki/internal/incidents/1988881234-onboard-warmup-thrash
maya: thanks team. Keep updates brief here. I'll post final unblock when shadow looks stable. :white_check_mark:
